title: How Many Stamps Does a Letter Need in Canada?
description: One Permanent stamp covers a letter up to 30 g. Heavier and oversize letters need two to six. The stamp count for each weight band.
keywords: how many stamps for a letter canada
how many stamps do i need canada
how many stamps to mail a letter in canada
answer: One Permanent stamp ($1.24) mails a standard letter up to 30 grams within Canada. A 30 to 50 gram letter needs two. Oversize letters need three stamps up to 100 grams and up to six at 500 grams. Weigh the envelope if it feels heavy; about five sheets of paper is near the 30 gram line.

blocks.p: Canada Post's rates are not multiples of the $1.24 Permanent stamp, so you round up to the next whole stamp. The table shows the postage required and the stamps that cover it.
Two stamps for a 30 to 50 g letter means paying $0.73 more than the rate. Stamps in other denominations can bring that closer to $1.75.

Ordinary 20 lb paper (75 g/m²) weighs about 4.5 g a sheet in US Letter size, and a light envelope about 6 g. Five sheets in an envelope come to roughly 28 g; a sixth sheet pushes it past 30 g. These are estimates. If the total is close to a band edge, weigh it on a kitchen scale, because an envelope that is one gram over is a different price.
Thick paper, a heavy envelope, or an insert such as a cheque or a card all add weight. Coloured stock and 24 lb paper are heavier than 20 lb.

sections.h2: What goes wrong when you are short

blocks.p: A letter with too little postage can come back to the sender. See [what happens to a letter with too little postage](/blog/letter-with-too-little-postage). It is the reason sendletter counts stamps from a deliberately heavy weight estimate: one extra stamp costs $1.24, and a short one risks the letter coming back.
